claim_being_audited: That the current release can be certified now as policy-compliant and evidentially supported based on aggregate readiness, rehearsal results, governance guidance, and contextual prior approval/monitoring, despite the current developer-support migration subgroup regression.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation already reflects the current evaluation results and explicitly discloses the subgroup weakness, certification could be compliant.
If there is approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering the subgroup weakness before launch, certification could be compliant.
Absent current disclosure or approved mitigation, the policy threshold for certification is not met even if aggregate readiness passes.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release documentation or model card showing the developer-support migration weakness is explicitly disclosed and that current evaluation results are reflected.
Provide approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation documentation covering the named subgroup weakness if disclosure is not the chosen path.
Provide the materiality determination, if any, showing why this subgroup regression would not count as a material limitation for the named launch use case.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation.
The admissible record shows a current named subgroup regression in a launch use case: the developer-support migration slice is 1.1 percentage points below the warning threshold.
The record includes no attached disclosure language, no reviewed mitigation, and no approved risk acceptance for that current weakness.
Prior approval of the model family predates the current policy update and current eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release predicate.
The release-thread monitoring comment is informal context only and does not meet the policy requirement for reviewed mitigation or approved acceptance.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supported on the existing record without first showing updated current-release documentation or approved mitigation for the subgroup weakness.
That prior approval and informal post-launch monitoring meaningfully substitute for the policy-required current disclosure or approved mitigation.
